Corpus Christi Catholic Primary School
Christ the Redeemer Catholic Education Trust
Christ the Redeemer Catholic Education Trust
https://ctrcet.co.uk/
Corpus Christi Catholic Primary School is now part of the Christ the Redeemer Catholic Education Trust.
For more information please visit the trust's website here - Christ the Redeemer Catholic Education Trust (ctrcet.co.uk) and see the message below from the CEO:
It is with great excitement and enthusiasm that I welcome you, as the founding CEO, to the website of our new and quickly growing Multi-academy Trust.
Our Trust consists of Catholic schools, with big educational ambitions for our children and young people. The Trust serves over 3,000 children and more than 450 employees across our eight schools in three London boroughs — Kingston, Richmond and Wandsworth: St Osmund's and St Elizabeth's in Richmond; St Agatha's, Our Lady Immaculate, Corpus Christi, St Joseph's and Richard Challoner in Kingston; and Sacred Heart in Roehampton, Wandsworth.
The Christ the Redeemer Catholic Education Trust was established in 2024 with a clear mission: to bring together Catholic schools across Kingston, Richmond and Wandsworth to share expertise, resources and a commitment to outstanding education.
As a Multi-Academy Trust, we believe that schools are stronger together. By collaborating across our family of schools, we can offer our children and young people the very best in Catholic education — grounded in Gospel values and driven by high academic ambitions.
John Conway CEO – Christ the Redeemer Catholic Education Trust

Catholic Social Teaching
Catholic Social Teaching (CST) is rooted in Scripture, formed by the wisdom of Church leaders. It is our moral compass which helps guide us on how to live out our faith in the world. CST calls us as a school to work for the common good, help build a just society, uphold the dignity of human life and work for the justice and dignity of all of our brothers and sisters.
We, as God's family, are called to love our neighbours in every situation, especially our global neighbours living in poverty. Following in the footsteps of Christ, we hope to make present in our unjust and broken world, the justice, love and peace of God.

pageCache.pageTitle: Corpus Christi Catholic Primary School - Collective Worship
pageCache.text:
Corpus Christi Catholic Primary School
Our Catholic Faith
Collective Worship
Collective Worship
Class Services
Each class participates in celebrating their class Saint on their feast day. Early Years and Key Stage One plan and deliver a class service together and Key Stage Two attend mass at our local Church St Josephs.
Collective Worship
Pupil led collective worship
Each week, a group of children in each Key Stage Two class lead a collective worship session with their peers. Children reflect on gospel stories as well as lead prayers, songs and other chosen activities. The children select the Bible reading that they want their session to be focused upon. They may choose a text related to the liturgical calendar, their class saint or a theme they would like their class to reflect upon e.g friendship, honesty or forgiveness. Through music, drama, prayer and reflection the children deliver their response to the Bible scripture they have listened to.
The sessions are structured around the following parts:
Gather - children gather together with a focus area. They can use candles, rosary beads and other religious artefacts. Some children may choose to hold their collective worship in other areas than their classroom such as the chapel, nature garden or outdoors.
Listen (to the Word) - children chose a Bible reading linked to their prayer theme
Respond - Children choose one or two ways to respond to the reading. For example, they may ask each child to write down a prayer or a promise and put each paper together in a jar. They could place this jar on the class prayer table as a constant reminder for the children throughout the week.
Go Forth/Mission - Children choose a way to go forth, sharing the Good News and following God's mission in their everyday lives. This can be telling others what they've heard, writing a poem or raising awareness.

pageCache.pageTitle: Corpus Christi Catholic Primary School - Our Catholic Faith
pageCache.text:
Corpus Christi Catholic Primary School
Our Catholic Faith
Our Catholic Faith
At Corpus Christi School we aim to give children a deeper knowledge and understanding of their Catholic faith. The religious, spiritual and moral education of the children is given high priority here. Religious education is more than a curriculum subject, it is something that guides every area of our school. As a Catholic school we aim to educate the whole child and our ethos is inseparable from the curriculum.
We are all part of the Body of Christ
At Corpus Christi Catholic Primary School, we are proud to be part of a vibrant, faith-filled community where Christ is at the heart of everything we do. Guided by Gospel values, our mission is to nurture each child’s spiritual, academic, and personal development in a caring and inclusive environment. We aim to inspire a lifelong love of learning while fostering a deep sense of respect, compassion, and responsibility. Rooted in our Catholic faith, our ethos promotes unity, service, and a commitment to living out our faith through action, ensuring that every child is supported to grow in confidence, character, and faith.
As a Catholic school our faith permeates every aspect of our school. Religion is a relationship of love between the child and God, and between the child and other people, in our community. Religious Education fosters this relationship through daily prayer, Acts of Worship and Celebrations of Liturgy. As a Catholic school we feel it is important that children learn how to co-operate with and forgive others. Scripture, teachings of the Church and the teachers’ own witness and example are the means by which these are taught.
From this September, Religious Education will be taught using a new Catholic RE Programme called 'Lighting the Path' publish by Oxford University Press and approved by the Archdiocese of Southwark. The implementation of the new programme will be phased over the next two academic years.
Children in the Early Years and Key Stage One will be taught using Lighting the Path from this September, followed by all Key Stage Two classes in September 2026.
Lighting the Path follows a spiral curriculum which means that each year group follows the same broad theme, but the content differs depending on the age of the pupils.
Years Three, Four, Five and Six will continue to follow Come and See Programme until the implementation in September 2026.
The priests of our parishes regularly visit the school, and are a link with the wider community of the Church.
At Corpus Christi Primary School we have a daily Collective Act of Worship. This involves the school community coming together, as a school, key stage or class group, and is a valuable part of our school day. On many Fridays the children of a class lead us in an assembly, and parents are welcome to attend.
We celebrate Mass as a community always on Holy days, and throughout the school year. We welcome parents and other parishioners to join us on these occasions. Our Feast day for Corpus Christi is always celebrated at school with our First Holy Communicants leading us in prayer at Mass.

pageCache.pageTitle: Corpus Christi Catholic Primary School - Governors
pageCache.text:
Corpus Christi Catholic Primary School
Governors
The purpose of this page is to introduce you to the Governors of Corpus Christi, and tell you about their role and responsibilities.
“In a Catholic school or college, the governors are the ‘Keepers of the Catholic Vision’, supporting and collaborating with teachers and chaplains in cultivating an authentic Catholic ethos……….Being a governor is not an inspectorial, or simply administrative role, but involves an attentive, committed monitoring of the life of the school” (Fit for Mission? Bishop of Lancaster)
The Governing Body has a strategic role in the leadership and management of the school. This means that it sets out:
Governors’ responsibilities include ensuring effective recruitment and staffing, robust delivery of the curriculum; upkeep of the premises, ensuring the health and safety of pupils and staff and setting and monitoring of the budget.
COMPOSITION OF GOVERNING BODY
The governing Body is made up of:
Governors serve for a term of 4 years. At the end of their term of office, they may be re-elected or re- appointed, provided they still meet the relevant criteria (e.g. Parent Governor still has a child at the school).
From September 2026 there are two governors’ committees which meet on a regular basis:
The Educational Standards and Catholic Life Committee: ensures that all matters relating to the school’s curriculum, including with regard to statutory requirements and the school’s curriculum policies are met, with the aim of raising standards of achievement for all children at the school along with playing a significant role in ensuring that the Catholic ethos permeates all aspects of school life and that it is accountable to the children, parents, staff and local community that it serves.
The Resources Committee: sets draft budgets for approval by the Governing Body; monitors the revenue budget and capital expenditure; ensures the premises are properly maintained; oversees building development projects; is a responsible for recruitment and staffing and sets out and monitors health and safety procedures.
Until academisation, there were three committees; The Curriculum Committee, The Resources Committee and The Faith, Families and Community Committee.
Other committees (e.g. Admissions Committee, Pay Committee) meet as and when required.
In addition to committee membership, each governor has responsibility for an area of the curriculum or of school life. Governors visit the school regularly to keep themselves informed of developments in their area of responsibility, and report back to the Governing Body.
Responsibility for discharging the functions of governors rests with the governing body as a whole, and governors cannot act as individuals. If you have any concerns relating to school matters you should therefore raise them with the Head Teacher or school staff.
However, if you would like to talk to any of the governors about their role, the school office staff will be happy to put you in touch.

pageCache.text:
Corpus Christi Catholic Primary School
Governor's Fund
At our school, we pride ourselves on providing a rich, vibrant, and nurturing environment for your children. However, as I am sure you have seen in the news, school budgets across the country are under immense pressure. Our finances are incredibly tight, and we are working harder than ever to ensure that these rising costs do not impact the quality of education and the extracurricular experiences we offer.
Many of you may remember supporting us in the past through what was known as the Governors Fund, often via an annual cheque or cash payment. To make things simpler for both parents and our small administrative team, we are moving this process over to a monthly Direct Debit system.
We are asking if you would consider setting up a monthly donation per child to the Governors Fund.
We are acutely aware that the "cost of living" remains a challenge for many families, and we want to be clear: there is absolutely no obligation to contribute. We only ask that you give if you feel you are in a position to do so.
Whether it is the price of a cup of coffee or a slightly larger amount, every penny stays within the school. These funds are vital for:
If you are a UK taxpayer, we can also claim Gift Aid on your donations. This is a fantastic way to boost your contribution at no extra cost to you; for every £1 you donate, the school receives an extra 25p from the government. Over the course of a year, this makes a significant difference to our bottom line.
Please click the link below to sign up to the direct debit scheme of your choice:
